dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that on classifier JOB failure the full fallback route should still run to completion even though the vote is forced to failure (or make the full jobs also require classify success so they don't run pointlessly).
evidence: gerrit-verify.yaml:467-468: `${{ ( needs.classify.result == 'success' && (` gates the entire success branch
full jobs use `if: ... && (needs.classify.result != 'success' || needs.classify.outputs.route == 'full')` (e.g. gerrit-verify.yaml:222) so they DO run when classify failed

CONTRIBUTING.md:207: 'A classifier failure also starts the full fallback route and still blocks `Verified`' — documents the block, but the full jobs still consume runner time with no chance of a green vote
dropped.finding: On a classifier JOB failure (needs.classify.result != 'success'), the full fallback jobs run per each full job's `if`, but the vote's CONCLUSION expression requires `needs.classify.result == 'success'` as a precondition for BOTH route branches, so the vote is forced to 'failure' even when every full fallback job succeeds. The full route is therefore executed to completion yet can never yield Verified+1 when the classifier job failed.
scenarios: Transient failure in the classify job (checkout/fetch/deepen error not caught by the classifier's own fail-closed path) — full lane runs ~7 jobs, all pass, yet Verified is -1 and a recheck is required.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (and document at the action's execution site) that every script/test the docs-only lane runs comes only from paths the classifier forces to full, so patchset code cannot execute in the reduced lane.
evidence: classify job comment gerrit-verify.yaml:117-119 asserts the classifier and allowlist come from trusted main
action.yml runs patchset-tree scripts, e.g. `python scripts/check_dco_identity.py` (action.yml ~line 70) and `python -m pytest ... "${doc_tests[@]}"` (action.yml:161)

Safety depends on classify_gerrit_verify_change.is_documentation_path returning FULL for any scripts/*.py or tests/*.py change (classify_gerrit_verify_change.py:51-61) — a correct but load-bearing invariant not asserted where the scripts run
dropped.finding: In the docs-only lane the composite action runs gate scripts sourced from the PATCHSET tree (scripts/check_dco_identity.py, scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py, gen_*.py, and `python -m pytest` over patchset test files), while only the route CLASSIFIER is checked out from trusted main. The security comment on the classify job ('a patchset cannot classify itself') covers routing but not the gate execution; the trust argument relies entirely on the fact that any change to these scripts/tests would classify as `full`.
scenarios: Any future widening of the allowlist (e.g. a docs-adjacent .py under docs/) would let patchset-controlled Python execute in the reduced lane.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral test that evaluates the vote CONCLUSION routing decision (docs-only complete, full complete, partial, mixed, classifier-failed) and asserts the fail-closed 'failure' outcome, rather than only asserting substrings of the GHA expression.
evidence: tests/unit/test_gerrit_docs_only.py:207-213 assert only that strings like "needs.classify.result=='success'" and "needs.{name}.result=='skipped'" appear in the normalized CONCLUSION expression text

gerrit-verify.yaml CONCLUSION is a multi-branch boolean (docs-only route all-skipped-full vs full route all-success-docs-skipped) `&& env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION || 'failure'` — the observable contract is which combinations yield failure, none of which is exercised

ABSENCE: no test evaluates the routing/aggregation outcome for a mixed-route or partial-route or classifier-failure input; the assertions are pure change-detectors on expression wording and pass regardless of the operators between the pinned tokens
dropped.finding: The vote job's new fail-closed CONCLUSION aggregation (require exactly one complete route; force 'failure' on partial route, mixed routes, or classifier failure) is only asserted via substring presence in the GHA expression text, not by exercising the boolean decision. A regression that weakens the logic (e.g. an inverted operator, a dropped `== 'skipped'` conjunct, or an OR that lets a half-completed route pass) would leave every substring present and the test green, so the specific fail-closed behavior this diff introduces is untested.
